text: Manchester United have already proved Michael Carrick can fix them. That is what makes this start so alarming. He arrived in January, simplified the shape, lifted the team to third, and earned a permanent deal. Four months later, United had five points from five league games, lost to promoted Hull, lost at home to a Manchester City side reduced to ten men, and threw away a two-goal lead against Brighton in the League Cup. So what disappeared? Maybe nothing. Maybe the first recovery was real, but it only solved the easiest problem. Carrick gave United clarity. Now he has to build an identity that survives when the game stops looking comfortable. The important distinction is between a team that looks better because its roles are clearer and a team that has built answers for every opponent. Those are not the same thing. A short run can hide the difference because confidence turns loose balls into attacks and a compact block makes every decision feel obvious. The harder test arrives when the opponent refuses to give United those moments. That is the test this video is about.
